indian.headline: Indian markets closed higher on FPI buying surge and FMCG strength; Nifty consolidating near 25,000.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed higher on FPI buying surge and FMCG strength; Nifty consolidating near 25,000.
indian.brief: Sensex rose 0.63% and Nifty 50 gained 0.58%, with Bank Nifty up 0.89%, as foreign investors poured ₹84,290 crore into equities in November's first half.
why: Foreign portfolio investors bought $7.5 billion in Indian equities in November's first 10 trading days—the highest inflow in five years—reversing three months of selling and lifting sentiment across indices.
FMCG sector jumped 1.9%, outperforming most peers, as consumer staples benefited from the broad market rally driven by the FPI inflow.
Banking sector gained 0.9% and Bank Nifty rose 0.89%, supporting the overall market despite continued weakness in auto, pharma, metal, and realty sectors, which fell 1.3–1.5%.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities closed on an upbeat note on November 16, 2026, with the Sensex climbing 0.63% and Nifty 50 adding 0.58%, buoyed by a historic surge in foreign investor buying. The rally was driven by a remarkable ₹84,290 crore inflow from foreign portfolio investors in November's first half—the strongest monthly buying in five years—as global funds rotated out of AI-heavy Western stocks and into Indian equities. This reversal ended three consecutive months of FPI outflows and restored confidence in Dalal Street.

Within the market, performance was uneven. FMCG emerged as the day's clear winner, jumping 1.9%, while banking stocks supported the broader indices with a 0.9% gain. However, weakness persisted in defensive and cyclical sectors: auto, realty, pharma, and metals all fell 1.3–1.5%, suggesting profit-taking in earlier gainers. Nifty 50 remained above the psychologically important 25,000 level and held key moving averages, though analysts cautioned that the index shows exhaustion after sharp recent gains and may consolidate between 24,700 and 25,500 before the next leg of the rally.

us.headline: US markets mixed as tech sells off; Nvidia earnings and Fed minutes loom large this week.
us.lead: US markets mixed as tech sells off; Nvidia earnings and Fed minutes loom large this week.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.40%, Nasdaq dropped 0.91%, but Dow rose 0.10% on a cautious day.
why: Tech sector collapsed 2.0% as semiconductor concerns spread globally ahead of Nvidia's crucial earnings report.
Energy and Financials posted modest gains (+1.0% and +0.8%), offering some support to broader indices.
Japan's Nikkei fell on semiconductor weakness, signaling investor nervousness across global chip stocks before major earnings.
Intel's ongoing lawsuit and DRAM antitrust case against Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron weighed on chip confidence.
us.narrative:
US stock markets finished mixed on 16 November as technology shares took a beating while defensive sectors like Energy and Financials offered modest support. The Nasdaq sank 0.91% with the tech sector down 2.0%, driven largely by anxiety over Nvidia's looming earnings report—a moment Wall Street is watching closely since the company has anchored much of recent AI-driven gains. Internationally, Japan's Nikkei also fell as semiconductor shares slumped, reflecting similar caution across global markets ahead of key earnings and Federal Reserve minutes expected this week.

The weakness in chips reflects deepening uncertainty in the sector: Intel faces a shareholder lawsuit over its 29% stock plunge after hiding PC sales weakness, while Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are fighting an antitrust suit claiming price-fixing on memory chips. On the bright side, Apple's upcoming AI-powered smart glasses and India's ₹2,03,500 crore semiconductor manufacturing push signal long-term industry momentum. Investors are now holding their breath for Nvidia's earnings and the Fed's meeting minutes, hoping they'll steady the recent AI sell-off.
